description:
The surah that mentions the miracle of **The Night Journey**, wherein God transported His servant Muḥammad in a single night from the Sacred Mosque of Mecca to al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem, to show him some of His most wondrous signs. God caused Muhammad, in the space of a single night, to journey from Mecca to Jerusalem and from there to heaven and back again. It takes its name from this subject, as relating to the celestial journey (mi'rāj) of the Prophet, mentioned in verse 1 and again in verse 60. The surah is framed by references to the Children of Israel at the beginning, and to Pharaoh at the end. The bulk of the surah deals with the Quran as guidance and warning, Muḥammad, and the nature of prophecy, especially the fact that he is a human being and incapable himself of producing miracles. It also warns of Iblis's promise to tempt mankind and of the fate of the disbelievers, and it gives a series of commandments (verse 22 ff.).
The surah is also known as Glory, The Children of Israel

14.1: Or 'today you suffice as your own reckoner.'

23.1: That is, do not grumble or speak to them in an ill-tempered manner. _Uff_ is an interjection expressing displeasure and exasperation, indicating that one has been put out of patience.

29.1: That is, neither be miserly nor be a spendthrift.

33.1: Such as mutilating the body of the murderer, or killing someone other than the guilty person for the sake of vengeance.

57.1: Or 'Those whom they (i.e., the polytheists) invoke, themselves seek a recourse to their Lord….'

78.1: That is, from noon onwards, when the sun crosses the meridian.

85.1: Or 'the Spirit relates to the command of my Lord.' Or 'the Spirit proceeds from the command of my Lord.'
85.2: Or 'you have not been given of the knowledge except a little.'

104.1: Or 'when the promise of the Hereafter comes.'
104.2: Or 'We shall bring you all together.' Or 'We shall bring you from all places.'

translations.1: Immaculate is He who carried His servant on a journey by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque whose environs We have blessed, that We might show him some of Our signs. Indeed He is the All-hearing, the All-seeing.
translations.2: We gave Moses the Book, and made it a guide for the Children of Israel —[saying,] 'Do not take any trustee besides Me'—
translations.3: descendants of those whom We carried [in the ark] with Noah. Indeed he was a grateful servant.
translations.4: We revealed to the Children of Israel in the Book: 'Twice you will cause corruption on the earth, and you will perpetrate great tyranny.'
translations.5: So when the first occasion of the two [prophecies] came, We aroused against you Our servants possessing great might, and they ransacked [your] habitations, and the promise was bound to be fulfilled.
translations.6: Then We gave you back the turn [to prevail] over them, and We aided you with children and wealth, and made you greater in number,
translations.7: [saying,] 'If you do good, you will do good to your [own] souls, and if you do evil, it will be [evil] for them.' So when the occasion for the other [prophecy] comes, they will make your faces<{["F", 1]}> wretched, and enter the Temple just as they entered it the first time, and utterly destroy whatever they come upon.
translations.8: Maybe your Lord will have mercy on you, but if you revert, We [too] will revert, and We have made hell a prison for the faithless.
translations.9: Indeed this Qur'ān guides to what is most upright, and gives the good news to the faithful who do righteous deeds that there is a great reward for them.
translations.10: As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have prepared a painful punishment for them.
translations.11: Man prays for ill as [avidly as] he prays for good, and man is overhasty.
translations.12: We made the night and the day two signs. Then We effaced the sign of the night, and made the sign of the day lightsome that you may seek grace from your Lord and that you may know the number of years and the calculation [of time], and We have elaborated everything in detail.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.13: We have attached every person's omen to his neck, and We shall bring it out for him on the Day of Resurrection as a wide open book that he will encounter.
translations.14: 'Read your book! Today your soul suffices as your own reckoner.'<{["F", 1]}>
translations.15: Whoever is guided is guided only for [the good of] his own soul, and whoever goes astray, goes astray only to its detriment. No bearer shall bear another's burden. We do not punish [any community] until We have sent [it] an apostle.
translations.16: And when We desire to destroy a town We command its affluent ones [to obey Allah]. But they commit transgression in it, and so the word becomes due against it, and We destroy it utterly.
translations.17: How many generations We have destroyed since Noah! _Your_ Lord suffices as one well aware and percipient of His servants' sins.
translations.18: Whoever desires this transitory life, We expedite for him therein whatever We wish, for whomever We desire. Then We appoint hell for him, to enter it, blameful and spurned.
translations.19: Whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with an endeavour worthy of it, should he be faithful —the endeavour of such will be well-appreciated.
translations.20: To these and to those—to all We extend the bounty of _your_ Lord, and the bounty of _your_ Lord is not confined.
translations.21: _Observe_ how We have given some of them an advantage over some others; yet the Hereafter is surely greater in respect of ranks and greater in respect of relative merit.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.22: Do not set up another god besides Allah, or you will sit blameworthy, forsaken.
translations.23: _Your_ Lord has decreed that you shall not worship anyone except Him, and [He has enjoined] kindness to parents. Should they reach old age at your side —one of them or both— do not say to them, 'Fie!'<{["F", 1]}> And do not chide them, but speak to them noble words.
translations.24: Lower the wing of humility to them, out of mercy, and say, 'My Lord! Have mercy on them, just as they reared me when I was [a] small [child]!'
translations.25: Your Lord knows best what is in your hearts. Should you be righteous, He is indeed most forgiving toward penitents.
translations.26: _Give_ the relatives their [due] right, and the needy and the traveller [as well], but do not squander wastefully.
translations.27: Indeed the wasteful are brothers of satans, and Satan is ungrateful to his Lord.
translations.28: And if you have to overlook them [for now], seeking the mercy of your Lord which you expect [in the future], speak to them gentle words.
translations.29: Do not keep your hand chained to your neck, nor open it altogether,<{["F", 1]}> or you will sit blameworthy, regretful.
translations.30: Indeed your Lord expands the provision for whomever He wishes, and tightens it. Indeed He is well aware and percipient of His servants.
translations.31: Do not kill your children for the fear of penury: We will provide for them and for you. Killing them is indeed a great iniquity.
translations.32: Do not approach fornication. It is indeed an indecency and an evil way.
translations.33: Do not kill a soul [whose life] Allah has made inviolable, except with due cause, and whoever is killed wrongfully, We have certainly given his heir an authority. But let him not commit any excess in killing,<{["F", 1]}> for he enjoys the support [of law].
translations.34: Do not approach the orphan's property except in the best manner until he comes of age. And fulfill the covenants; indeed all covenants are accountable.
translations.35: When you measure, observe fully the measure, [and] weigh with an even balance. That is better and fairer in outcome.
translations.36: Do not follow that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed the hearing, the eyesight, and the heart —all of these are accountable.
translations.37: Do not walk exultantly on the earth. Indeed you will neither pierce the earth, nor reach the mountains in height.
translations.38: The evil of all these is detestable to _your_ Lord.
translations.39: These are among [precepts] that _your_ Lord has revealed to _you_ of wisdom. Do not set up another god besides Allah, or you will be cast into hell, blameworthy, banished.
translations.40: Did your Lord prefer you for sons, and [Himself] adopt females from among the angels?<{["F", 1]}> Indeed you say a monstrous word!
translations.41: Certainly We have paraphrased [the principles of guidance] in this Qur'ān so that they may take admonition, but it increases them only in aversion.
translations.42: _Say_, 'Were there [other] gods besides Him, as they say, they would surely encroach on the Lord of the Throne.
translations.43: Immaculate is He, and greatly exalted above what they say!'
translations.44: The seven heavens glorify Him, and the earth [too], and whoever is in them. There is not a thing but celebrates His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed He is all-forbearing, all-forgiving.
translations.45: When _you_ recite the Qur'ān, We draw between _you_ and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden curtain,
translations.46: and We cast veils on their hearts, lest they should understand it, and a deafness into their ears. When _you_ mention _your_ Lord alone in the Qur'ān, they turn their backs in aversion.
translations.47: We know best what they listen for, when they listen to _you_, and when they hold secret talks, when the wrongdoers say, '[If you follow him] You will be following just a bewitched man.'
translations.48: _Look_, how they coin epithets for _you_; so they go astray, and cannot find a way.
translations.49: They say, 'What, when we have become bones and dust, shall we really be raised in a new creation?'
translations.51: or a creature more fantastic to your minds!' They will say, 'Who will bring us back?' _Say_, 'He who originated you the first time.' They will nod their heads at you, and say, 'When will that be?' _Say_, 'Maybe it is near!
translations.52: The day He calls you, you will respond to Him, praising Him, and you will think you remained only a little.'
translations.53: _Tell_ My servants to speak in a manner which is the best. Indeed Satan incites ill feeling between them, and Satan is indeed man's manifest enemy.
translations.54: Your Lord knows you best. He will have mercy on you, if He wishes, or punish you, if He wishes, and We did not send _you_ to watch over them.
translations.55: Your Lord knows best whoever is in the heavens and the earth. Certainly We gave some prophets an advantage over others, and We gave David the Psalms.
translations.56: _Say_, 'Invoke those whom you claim [to be gods] besides Him. They have no power to remove your distress nor to bring about any change [in your state].
translations.57: They [themselves] are the ones who supplicate, seeking a recourse to their Lord,<{["F", 1]}> whoever is nearer [to Him], expecting His mercy and fearing His punishment.' Indeed _your_ Lord's punishment is a thing to beware of.
translations.58: There is not a town but We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection, or punish it with a severe punishment. That has been written in the Book.
translations.59: Nothing keeps Us from sending signs except that the ancients denied them. We gave Thamūd the she-camel as an eye-opener, but they wronged her. We do not send the signs except for deterrence.
translations.60: When We said to _you_, 'Indeed _your_ Lord comprehends all mankind,' We did not appoint the vision that We showed _you_ except as a test for the people and the tree cursed in the Qur'ān. We deter them, but it only increases them in great rebellion.
translations.61: When We said to the angels, 'Prostrate before Adam,' they [all] prostrated, but not Iblis: he said, 'Shall I prostrate before someone whom You have created from clay?'
translations.62: Said he, 'Do You see this one whom You have honoured above me? If You respite me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely destroy his progeny, [all] except a few.'
translations.63: Said He, 'Begone! Whoever of them follows you, indeed the hell shall be your requital, an ample reward.
translations.64: Instigate whomever of them you can with your voice;<{["F", 1]}> and rally against them your cavalry and your infantry, and share with them in wealth and children, and make promises to them!' But Satan promises them nothing but delusion.
translations.65: 'As for My servants, you shall have no authority over them.' And _your_ Lord suffices as trustee.
translations.66: Your Lord is He who drives for you the ships in the sea, that you may seek His grace. Indeed He is most merciful to you.
translations.67: And when distress befalls you at sea, those whom you invoke besides Him are forsaken. But when He delivers you to land, you are disregardful [of Him]. And man is very ungrateful.
translations.68: Do you feel secure that He will not make the coastland swallow you, or He will not unleash upon you a rain of stones? Then you will not find any defender for yourselves.
translations.69: Do you feel secure that He will not send you back into it another time and unleash against you a shattering gale and drown you because of your unfaith? Then you will not find for yourselves any redresser against Us.
translations.70: Certainly We have honoured the Children of Adam, and carried them over land and sea, and provided them with all the good things, and given them an advantage over many of those We have created with a complete preference.
translations.71: The day We shall summon every group of people with their _imam_,<{["F", 1]}> then whoever is given his book in his right hand —they will read it, and they will not be wronged so much as a single date-thread.
translations.72: But whoever has been blind in this [world], will be blind in the Hereafter, and [even] more astray from the [right] way.
translations.73: They were about to beguile _you_ from what Allah has revealed to _you_ so that _you_ may fabricate against Us something other than that, whereat they would have befriended _you_.
translations.74: Had We not fortified _you_, certainly _you_ might have inclined toward them a bit.
translations.75: Then We would have surely made _you_ taste a double [punishment] in this life and a double [punishment] after death, and then _you_ would have not found for _yourself_ any helper against Us.
translations.76: They were about to hound you out of the land, to expel you from it, but then they would not have stayed after you but a little.
translations.77: A precedent of those We have sent from among Our apostles before _you_, and _you_ will not find any change in Our precedent.
translations.78: Maintain the prayer from the sun's decline<{["F", 1]}> till the darkness of the night, and [_observe_ particularly] the dawn recital. Indeed the dawn recital is attended [by angels].
translations.79: And _keep vigil_ for a part of the night, as a supererogatory [devotion] for _you_. It may be that _your_ Lord will raise _you_ to a praiseworthy station.
translations.80: And _say_, 'My Lord! 'Admit me with a worthy entrance, and bring me out with a worthy departure, and render me a favourable authority from Yourself.'
translations.81: And _say_, 'The truth has come, and falsehood has vanished. Indeed falsehood is bound to vanish.'
translations.82: We send down in the Qur'ān that which is a cure and mercy for the faithful; and it increases the wrongdoers only in loss.
translations.83: When We bless man, he is disregardful and turns aside; but when an ill befalls him, he is despondent.
translations.84: _Say_, 'Everyone acts according to his character. Your Lord knows best who is better guided with regard to the way.'
translations.85: They question _you_ concerning the Spirit. _Say_, 'The Spirit is of the command of my Lord,<{["F", 1]}> and you have not been given of the knowledge except a few [of you].'<{["F", 2]}>
translations.86: If We wish, We would take away what We have revealed to _you_. Then _you_ would not find for _yourself_ any defender against Us,
translations.87: except a mercy from _your_ Lord. Indeed His grace has been great upon _you_.
translations.88: _Say_, 'Should all humans and jinn rally to bring the like of this Qur'ān, they will not bring the like of it, even if they assisted one another.'
translations.89: We have certainly interspersed for the people this Qur'ān with every [kind of] parable, but most people are only intent on ingratitude.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.90: They say, 'We will not believe you until _you_ make a spring gush forth for us from the ground.
translations.91: Or until _you_ have a garden of date palms and vines and _you_ make streams gush through it.
translations.92: Or until _you_ cause the sky to fall in fragments upon us, just as you would aver. Or until you bring Allah and the angels [right] in front of us.
translations.93: Or until _you_ have a house of gold, or _you_ ascend into the sky. And we will not believe _your_ ascension until _you_ bring down for us a book that we may read.' _Say_, 'Immaculate is my Lord! Am I anything but a human, an apostle?!'
translations.94: Nothing kept the people from believing when guidance came to them, but their saying, 'Has Allah sent a human as an apostle?!'
translations.95: _Say_, 'Had there been angels in the earth, walking around and residing [in it like humans do], We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as apostle.'
translations.96: _Say_, 'Allah suffices as a witness between me and you. Indeed He is well aware and percipient of His servants.'
translations.97: Whomever Allah guides is rightly guided, and whomever He leads astray _you_ will never find them any guardians besides Him. On the Day of Resurrection, We shall muster them [scrambling] on their faces,<{["F", 1]}> blind, dumb, and deaf. Their refuge shall be hell. Whenever it subsides, We shall intensify the blaze for them.
translations.98: That is their requital because they defied Our signs and said, 'What, when we have become bones and dust, shall we really be raised in a new creation?'
translations.99: Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the like of them? He has appointed for them a term, in which there is no doubt; yet the wrongdoers are only intent on ingratitude.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.100: _Say_, 'Even if you possessed the treasuries of my Lord's mercy, you would withhold them for the fear of being spent, and man is very niggardly.'
translations.101: Certainly We gave Moses nine manifest signs. So ask the Children of Israel. When he came to them, Pharaoh said to him, 'O Moses, indeed I think you are bewitched.'
translations.102: He said, 'You certainly know that no one has sent these [signs] except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as eye-openers, and I, O Pharaoh, indeed think you are doomed.'
translations.103: He desired to exterminate them from the land, so We drowned him and all those who were with him.
translations.104: After him We said to the Children of Israel, 'Take up residence in the land, and when the occasion of the other [promise] comes,<{["F", 1]}> We shall gather you in mixed company.'<{["F", 2]}>
translations.105: With the truth did We send it down, and with the truth did it descend, and We did not send _you_ except as a bearer of good news and as a warner.
translations.106: We have sent the Qur'ān in [discrete] parts so that _you_ may read it to the people a little at a time, and We have sent it down piecemeal.
translations.107: _Say_, 'Whether you believe in it, or do not believe in it, indeed those who were given knowledge before it when it is recited to them, fall down in prostration on their faces,
translations.108: and _say_, "Immaculate is our Lord! Indeed Our Lord's promise is bound to be fulfilled."
translations.109: Weeping, they fall down on their faces, and it increases them in humility.'
translations.110: _Say_, 'Invoke "Allah" or invoke "the All-beneficent." Whichever [of His Names] you may invoke, to Him belong the Best Names.' _Be neither_ loud in _your_ prayer, nor murmur it, but _follow_ a middle course between these,
translations.111: and _say_, 'All praise belongs to Allah, who has neither taken any son, nor has He any partner in sovereignty, nor has He [taken] any ally out of weakness,' and _magnify_ Him with a magnification [worthy of Him].
